pageCache.pageTitle: Woodberry Down Primary School - Outstanding Education in Woodberry Down
pageCache.text:
Headteacher Welcome
It is with great pleasure that we welcome you to Woodberry Down Community Primary School.
Set close to Finsbury Park in Hackney, our school is a three form entry primary school with approximately 700 children on roll. There are three classes in each year group of approximately 90 pupils. With a preschool provision, children between the ages of two and eleven attend our school.
At Woodberry Down, kindness and understanding are at the core of everything we do, fostering a proudly diverse and inclusive community. There truly is no place like Woodberry Down. With a focus on nurturing innovative and passionate learners, we are committed to providing every child with enriching, meaningful experiences that deepen their understanding of the world. Our broad and engaging curriculum is designed to spark curiosity, inspire imagination and empower our pupils to thrive.
At Woodberry Down, we are deeply committed to fostering a shared sense of responsibility within the wider school community. By providing high-quality education, we strive to improve life opportunities not only for our own pupils but also for those in the broader community. Collaboration lies at the heart of our approach, as we work closely with families and the local community to ensure every child flourishes.
We take pride in knowing and valuing each child as an individual, preparing them for the next steps in their education and equipping them for the challenges and joys of life ahead. At Woodberry Down, every child is encouraged to aim high, supported by dedicated staff who celebrate their achievements and inspire their growth.
Alongside Grazebrook, Shacklewell and Thomas Fairchild primary schools, we are well supported by a strong and experienced governing board who challenge leaders and staff to do all that they can for the pupils and the community.
Our website contains a wealth of information about the school and our partnership with our three sister schools. We update the website content regularly, and I ask that you check frequently to find out about our achievements, our plans and developments. If you cannot find the information that you need, we are always available to support.
You can contact the school office on 0208 800 5758 during working hours or can email us at wdoffice@newwavefederation.co.uk.

Careers
For over a decade we have built highly successful teams of professionals, driven by their commitment to the communities we serve. Our team is passionate, dedicated and committed to allowing each child to achieve their greatest potential.
A career at the New Wave Federation is both challenging and highly rewarding - an experience suited to people who are flexible, motivated and creative. We offer schools which are well resourced, have an established culture of excellence and are committed to personalised professional development. Our schools are vibrant, diverse and inclusive. If you are an effective communicator, have vision, energy and believe every child can and will succeed, we would like to hear from you.

Ofsted and Performance Results
Ofsted
Woodberry Down Primary School was most recently inspected on 5th and 6th December 2023 and we are incredibly proud of the outcomes and the continued growth of our school. Our success is a reflection of the hard work of our pupils, the dedication of our staff and the vital role of our wider community. We recognise that the support and care our children receive from families, local partners and everyone involved in our school life are key to helping them thrive and reach their full potential.
We are proud of the nurturing and inclusive environment we’ve built together, where every child is encouraged to succeed. To read the full inspection report, please click here.
Performance
We take immense pride in the achievements of our pupils and the excellent results of our school. Their hard work, determination and dedication reflect the supportive and inspiring learning environment we foster every day. At Woodberry Down, we celebrate the unique talents and successes of each pupil, knowing that their accomplishments are a testament to the strength of our school community.

Recruitment Fairs
Our schools are vibrant, diverse, and inclusive, and we’re looking for educators who are effective communicators, full of energy and believe every child can and will succeed. Whether you're an Early Career Teacher or an experienced educator seeking new challenges, New Wave Federation invites you to our upcoming Teacher Recruitment Events.​
Event Details
Join us at one of our fairs on the following dates:
Grazebrook Primary School
Thomas Fairchild Community School
Wednesday 30th April
Woodberry Down Community Primary School
What to Expect on the Day
Step inside our classrooms and corridors to see what makes our schools so special. You’ll get a real feel for our creative learning environments, welcoming culture and the way we bring the curriculum to life.
Hear directly from our inspirational Headteachers as they share the vision, values and ethos that shape our schools. Learn about our commitment to inclusion, high expectations and the ways we support both children and staff to excel.
Speak with our teaching team in an informal setting and find out what it’s really like to work here. From Early Career Teachers to experienced leaders, you’ll hear honest reflections on their day-to-day work, the support they receive and the professional development that’s helped them grow.
Bring your questions and we’ll do our best to answer them. Whether you’re curious about the application process, the structure of our teams, CPD opportunities or work-life balance, we’re here to give you the clarity and confidence to take the next step in your teaching career
Apply for a job today
For detailed information about our Federation, staff benefits and the application process, download our Application Pack and Application form.
Why Choose New Wave Federation?
All of our schools are rated Good or Outstanding by Ofsted and share a strong commitment to delivering exceptional, modern teaching. Classrooms are well resourced and our use of iPads and digital tools enhances learning across the curriculum. You’ll have the freedom to be creative, backed by the tools and infrastructure to make it happen.
You’ll become part of a federation-wide team of passionate professionals who plan, reflect and grow together. Our culture is one of openness, shared ambition and mutual support.
We value your growth as much as our pupils’. With tailored CPD, coaching and clear career development pathways, you’ll be supported at every stage of your journey, whether you’re newly qualified or looking to step into leadership.
Our schools proudly reflect the vibrant communities of Hackney. We celebrate diversity in all its forms and champion an inclusive environment where every staff member and every child feels seen, heard and valued.
For further enquiries about the events or application process, please contact llangley@newwavefederation.co.uk.​
We look forward to welcoming you to the New Wave Federation and exploring the possibilities together.​

pageCache.pageTitle: Woodberry Down Primary - Reading at Woodberry Down
pageCache.text:
Reading at Woodberry Down
Reading is at the heart of our curriculum at Woodberry Down. We empower children to be fluent and confident readers through a structured and creative English curriculum with high-quality texts at its heart.
Alongside technical reading skills, we place great emphasis on reading for pleasure and endeavour to develop a lifelong love of reading in our children. Teachers read to their pupils every day and children are motivated to read widely both inside and outside of school.
At New Wave, we have created reading pathways to develop children's reading in lessons, at home and when reading for pleasure so that every child sees themselves as a reader. Within each year group, multiple copies of core reading for pleasure books are available for children to read, enjoy and discuss. You can view these texts in the links below. Alongside these each class reading area has a wide selection of texts which include picture books, novels, short chapter books, graphic novels, poetry anthologies and non-fiction texts.
Nursery
In Nursery, we follow a book-based curriculum. Each topic that they learn is linked to a high quality and engaging picture book as well as non-fiction texts. They also enjoy daily storytime, so all children are read a story at least once every day. Our team is highly skilled in prompting child-led book talk when reading to encourage early language development and instil a passion for books.
Reception
The curriculum in reception is underpinned by a book based approach. All learning is linked to a high quality and engaging picture book as well as non-fiction texts. Story time is timetabled every day so that children can enjoy at least one story each day. Our team is highly skilled in prompting child-led book talk when reading to encourage early language development and instil a passion for books.
Year 1
In Year 1, children look forward to their daily story time. Teachers select books that children will look forward to and love. These carefully selected books will also expose them to new words to extend and deepen children’s vocabulary.
Year 2
In Year 2, children look forward to their daily story time. Teachers select books that children will look forward to and love. These carefully selected books will also expose them to new words to extend and deepen children’s vocabulary.
Year 3
In Year 3 children collectively read a class novel each day. Twice a week they enjoy DEAR (Drop Everything and Read). This is 20 minutes of dedicated time for children to read a book of their choice, and it reinforces the importance of making time for reading.
Year 4
In Year 4 children collectively read a class novel each day. Twice a week they enjoy DEAR (Drop Everything and Read). This is 20 minutes of dedicated time for children to read a book of their choice, and it reinforces the importance of making time for reading.
Year 5
In Year 5 children read a class novel daily. Twice a week they enjoy DEAR (Drop Everything and Read). This is 20 minutes of dedicated time for children to read a book of their choice, and it reinforces the importance of making time for reading. Chatterbooks Book Club is also available for children to help build a lifelong reading habit.
Year 6
In Year 6 children read a class novel daily. Twice a week they enjoy DEAR (Drop Everything and Read). This is 20 minutes of dedicated time for children to read a book of their choice, and it reinforces the importance of making time for reading. Chatterbooks Book Club is also available for children to help build a lifelong reading habit.

pageCache.pageTitle: Woodberry Down Primary - After School Activity Clubs
pageCache.text:
After School Activity Clubs
We have a good choice of clubs available for families to choose from each term. Clubs range from drama and dance to sports and pottery. Children really enjoy the clubs; both for what the club is offering and for the social aspects.
We work closely with our providers to ensure children get the best possible experience each week delivered by committed and quality tutors and coaches. Where possible these tutors and coaches are also supported by existing Woodberry Down staff members.
Clubs run from 3.30pm until 4.45pm (unless stated otherwise). 3.30pm – 3.45pm is snack time; please provide your child with a light healthy snack. If your child attends a dance or sports-based club please do send them to school, on the day of their club, in their PE kit.
Summer Term – Clubs can now be purchased.
Please purchase via MCAS if you are interested.
Football – Y1/2 - Y3/4
Provider: Woodberry Down CPS
The benefits of our football clubs are that they are fun and social and that can boost your child's confidence, improve team work, learn new skills and meet new friends. We aim to help children improve on skills such as dribbling, passing, receiving, shooting, awareness, team work, decision making and tricks to get past opponents.
All football clubs are run by school-based coaches that I am sure you all know very well.
Arts & Crafts Rec/Y1/2/3
Provider: Chien Kids Creative Emporium
We are Chien Kids Creative Emporium. We run the arts n crafts clubs. We train little hands to accomplish big things!
“Once you discover one simple fact, and that is, everything around you called life, was made up by people who were no smarter than you and you can change it, you can influence it, you can build your own things that other people can use.”
Steve Jobs, Founder of Apple Inc.
We believe children learn by doing, by accomplishing their little project and quickly developing hands on skills and problem-solving skills.
We are excited to bring in lots of different projects for children to enjoy and create!
Drama
After drama classes exploring storytelling, script work and drama games in a fun and supportive environment. A place for children to build confidence, teamwork and creative skills. This term children will work towards an end of term show for parents to come and enjoy. Details will be shared closer to the date of the performance
Non-Contact Boxing
Provider: A Plus Fit
We provide a safe and controlled environment for the children to learn not only the art of boxing but also to access the benefits that come with it.
Coach Ash - a former pupil of Woodberry Down Community School, comes from a Boxing background and is currently a Level 3 Personal Trainer. He uses his experience in coaching juniors and professional skill to deliver and build a fun, interactive club.
The benefits of boxing:
- Increases motor skills such as balance, coordination, speed, agility and overall movement key to everyday living.
- Improves cardio level for a healthier heart and lungs.
- Provides a better self-defence.
- A form of controlled expression for the children.
Our Non-Contact Boxing requires a high level of respect from the children for the coach and each other, we practice listening, assisting and trusting one and other in each session which provides a newly found dimension of thoughtfulness and awareness amongst the group that can be used in everyday life.
Football Y5/6
After School Football Fun!
Come and join our awesome after school football club! Our super-friendly FA qualified coaches will help you learn cool tricks, score amazing goals, and play loads of exciting games. Whether you’re a beginner or a future football star, you’ll have fun, make new friends, and be part of a great team. Don’t miss out!
Girls Rugby Y3/4/5/6
Fencing
Provider: Little Musketeers

Lego
Provider: Bonne Idée
Would you like to be part of the fun and creative world of Lego? Lego club helps to improve focus and concentration, increase spatial awareness, develop fine motor skills, encourage lateral thinking and creative problem solving, inspire experimentation and adventure, teach organization skills and patience. Kind regards,
Beginner Cycling Club
Provider: Cycling Club Hackney
This club is primarily aimed at children who cannot yet ride a bike. We also welcome children who can ride but may lack confidence or experience.
The club operates in cycles, with our main goal being to help as many children as possible learn to ride confidently. Once your child is considered a confident rider, we will inform you, and their place will be offered to another child on the waiting list.
To make the most of our time with the children, group sizes are kept small. If your registration is not successful, your child will be placed on our waiting list.
Helmets are compulsory. If your child has their own helmet, they must use it. We also have a limited number of helmets available at school for children to borrow.
We ask that all participants wear suitable clothing, and that hairstyles take into consideration the need to wear a helmet comfortably and safely.
Please note that weather can be a significant factor. While we will do our best to continue in light rain, sessions will be cancelled if conditions are deemed too wet or unsafe. Families will be informed of any cancellations as early as possible.
Animation
Provider: London Lens Project
Join the Adventure at Animation Club! 🌟
Unlock the door to a world where your imagination leaps off the page and onto the screen! At Animation Club, students dive into the magic of animation, transforming their creative ideas into vivid, moving stories. With access to handheld cameras and an innovative editing suite, the possibilities are endless. From crafting voiceovers to adding dynamic music, titles, text, and sound effects, our young animators will learn to fine-tune their masterpieces with tools designed to unleash their full creative potential.
🌈 What's Inside the Animator's Studio?
- State-of-the-Art Equipment: Shoot your animations with smart cameras and edit like a pro in our user-friendly, creative suite. All equipment is provided by us!
- Creative Freedom: Add voiceovers, music, titles, text, and sound effects. Play with speed adjustments, green screens and filters to bring your vision to life.
- Showcase Your Creations: All animations are securely saved on Google Drive, allowing parents to access their child's imaginative worlds.
🎥 Dive Deep into the World of Animation
- Human Animations: Experience the thrill of being in front and behind the camera, mastering the core principles of animation while fostering teamwork.
- Software Mastery: Experiment with music, voiceovers, filters, and backgrounds to enhance your storytelling.
- Claymation Magic: Design and morph Playdoh characters, exploring the fundamentals of animation through tactile creativity.
- Lego Animation: Unleash your storytelling through Lego, constructing your designs and bringing stories to life with magic tricks and illusions.
Whether you're sketching out your first character or piecing together a complex scene, our club offers a supportive and enriching environment for every young animator. No experience? No problem! All equipment is provided, ensuring each student has the tools they need to succeed from day one.
📽️ Discover More About Our Animated Adventures
Curious about what makes our Animation Exploration Club so special? Watch this short 1-minute video to see our animators in action, from drawing and software voiceovers to character design with Playdoh and Lego storytelling. Experience firsthand the joy and creativity that comes from bringing your ideas to life.
Dodgeball Club:
Provider: Woodberry Down CPS
Get ready to dive into the most exciting after-school activity—DODGEBALL! Sign up for our Dodgeball Club and experience all the fun, fast-paced action while making new friends and improving your teamwork skills. Dodgeball is the perfect way to stay active, boost your coordination, and sharpen your reflexes. Plus, dodging and throwing help build strength and endurance. Whether you're an expert or a total beginner, everyone is welcome to join the fun! Don't miss out—let's dodge, duck, and throw our way to victory!

Our Hip Hop Freestyle Afterschool Club is a high-energy, fun-filled session designed to get children moving and expressing themselves.
We focus on freestyle and individuality, helping each child develop their own style rather than following strict routines. It’s all about creativity, confidence, and enjoying dance in a supportive environment. Perfect for all abilities, every session is packed with music, movement, and fun

Curriculum
Our curriculum is the planned experiences and interactions our children encounter every day. It is designed to be enriching and stimulating, whilst meeting and exceeding the expectations set out in the national curriculum.
The implementation of our curriculum is complemented by a wide choice of resources such as iPads, mathematical equipment and a wide range of texts in English. We utilise the skills of our teachers to inspire all of our pupils to achieve their full potential. We value cross curricular learning and by closely assessing what skills each academic discipline requires, we can create strong links between core and non-core subjects.
We aim to develop curious and confident learners and ensure all pupils have opportunities to achieve high standards. Our curriculum is designed to develop a capacity to accommodate new knowledge building on prior knowledge and experiences, resulting in curious minds.
At Woodberry Down Primary School we believe that all children are entitled to equality of opportunity within all subjects irrespective of race, gender, sexual orientation, religious belief, physical or mental condition or background.
We are committed to providing a curriculum that is appropriate to, and meets the needs of, every child, enabling each to reach their full potential. Teachers provide learning opportunities that are matched to the needs of our children, including children with special educational needs and disability as well as those that are identified as being more able and talented.
Our Provision

pageCache.text:
Free School Meals
All primary school children who attend state schools in London receive Free School Meals and have done so since September 2023. This means that no pupils at Woodberry Down need to pay for school meals.
However, your child may also be eligible for extra funding for our school from the government, worth £1,300 per year. This is extra money for us to spend on enrichment activities, teacher development and targeted support for the children that need it most. This may also entitle you to other benefits like food vouchers during the holidays. We urge our families to apply for free school meals so that we can continue to provide the high standard of education and extended provision that we currently offer.
If you feel your child is entitled to Free School Meals, you must apply by completing an application form. You only have to apply once. Hackney Education will check your entitlement against information held by the Department for Education on a regular basis so that you don’t have to renew your application every year or provide proof of your entitlement.
After you have completed your application you will receive an email to confirm your eligibility. You can then bring this into the school office as proof of your entitlement. Hackney Education will also send out a notification to us here at school confirming your child’s FSM and Pupil Premium eligibility.

Parent Council
The Woodberry Down Parent Council is a small group of parent representatives from a range of year groups across the school. It is intended that, at the start of each school year, a representative is sought from each year group to join the group. Parents are invited to nominate themselves for the role or to suggest a member of the parent community for the position.
The group was created to give the families at the school the opportunities to express their views, opinions and ideas. We seek to involve our families in the quest to raise standards and achievements and to improve provision within the school.
The group meets six times per year, once per half term. In advance of each meeting, an agenda is agreed by the council members and school staff through taking items suggested by the wider school community for discussion. The group also meets to participate in learning walks and meetings with the student council during the school year.
Actions taken as a result of discussions and suggestions in meetings are shared with the wider community through letters from senior leaders. Initiatives such as Come Dine with Me and additional family support sessions have been introduced as a result of the dedication of the group.

pageCache.text:
Pupil Leadership Groups
At Woodberry Down, we value the positive contributions children can make to school life. We encourage our pupils to play an active role in decisions and empower them to have an impact on the school community. Pupil Groups are formed of elected children who take responsibility for different aspects of our school's provision.
Adults and children collaborate for school improvement.
Learning Council
Visits other classes to look at learning activities.
Observes learning in lessons and comments on them from the children's point of view
Carries out pupil voice surveys on different aspects of school life.
Reviews the school’s curriculum offer.
Makes recommendations to governors, leadership and teaching teams.
Reading Ambassadors
Promote a love of reading across the school, including reading to younger children.
Gather pupil voice about recommended reads and share these with leaders.
Help the adults ensure reading is across the whole curriculum.
Are responsible for maintaining inspiring book corners.
Playground Friends
Support and guide other children in the KS2 playground to use the playground areas in a responsible and friendly manner.
Help set up a zone of the playground and guide other children on how to use it appropriately.
Look after equipment and designated areas.
Support the adults to create and maintain a fun relaxing atmosphere at playtime that all children can enjoy.
Commit for a day every week to fulfil their responsibilities as a playground friend.
